correctness.summary: The covering number is forced by a representative K_{h,l} and attained by the cluster-pair cover. The partition lower bound is the Erdos--Faudree--Ordman cut inequality. A balanced assignment of first-side internal edges to second-side clusters yields edge-disjoint K4s; remaining second-side internal edges fit into unused cluster pairs as triangles, and all remaining crossing edges are 2-cliques. The capacity hypotheses guarantee every assignment. The resulting partition has exactly s-2a-b members. The asymptotic exact-order choice satisfies the hypotheses and gives coefficient 3/2^(5/3).

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Ning's 2026 preprint proves d_n=Theta(n^(4/3)) and treats the balanced uniform family (hK_k) join (hK_k) for even k, followed by isolated-vertex padding. The cut inequality is prior work. Searches under clique partition/covering, joins of cluster graphs, unequal clique clusters, cographs, and related decomposition language found no prior heterogeneous formula of this form and no explicit all-order limsup coefficient 3/2^(5/3). Older differently phrased decomposition literature and recent unindexed work remain residual risks.

value.summary: The mixed family absorbs exact-order remainders inside cluster sizes, permits asymmetric cluster scales, and sharpens the known construction quantitatively to the explicit uniform bound limsup d_n/n^(4/3) <= 3/2^(5/3) approximately 0.9449407874. The finite theorem also supplies a reusable exact-attainment criterion for a natural cluster-join cograph family.

limitations: The capacity conditions are sufficient and are not claimed necessary.
The numerical coefficient is an explicit construction upper bound, not a proof of the optimal asymptotic constant.
The Theta(n^(4/3)) order and the cut lower bound are prior results and are not claimed as new.
Older literature under different clique-decomposition terminology and very recent unindexed work remain residual originality risks.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the symbolic proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
